title: Enterprise Onboarding — Integration, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Comprehensive playbook for enterprise customer onboarding covering technical integration, escalation procedures, known issues and workarounds, support process, and health-check/QBR cadence.
body:
INTRODUCTION

Purpose
This document describes the standardized, cross-functional playbook used by Redwood Inference customer success (CS), support, solutions engineering (SE), and SRE teams to onboard enterprise customers. It consolidates the integration checklist, escalation ladder, known issues and mitigations, ongoing support process, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) materials to ensure reliable, predictable, and measurable onboarding outcomes.

Scope
- Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated, Private, and high-usage Hosted tiers).
- Includes technical integration, operational readiness, escalation and incident handling, and ongoing health/QBR cadence.

Audience
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers and Implementation Engineers
- Support Engineers and SREs
- Sales & Account teams for handoff

OWNERSHIP & CONTACTS

Primary owner: Customer Success
Document author: Aisha Patel
Reviewers: Liam O'Connor; Chen Wang; Maria Gomez
Escalation contacts:
- Support Level 1 (CS Support): support-enterprise@redwood.ai
- Solutions Engineering (prod integration): se-enterprise@redwood.ai
- SRE / Platform on-call: SRE-oncall (pager duty link in dashboards)
- Enterprise account executive: assigned per account

CONFIDENTIALITY: internal

TIMELINE & PHASES

1. Pre-kickoff (Sales -> CS handoff)
- Deliverables: signed contract, SSO/KMS requirements, data residency needs, security questionnaire answers, and account contact list.
- Action: CS schedules Kickoff and Implementation workshop within 3 business days of handoff.

2. Kickoff (Week 0)
- Participants: CSM, SE, customer technical lead, security/infra contacts, account exec.
- Agenda: rollout goals, success metrics, network & security requirements, integration plan, data flows, and project timeline.

3. Integration & Validation (Weeks 1-4)
- Tasks: network configuration, auth keys/SSO, model selection & config, test prompts, traffic shaping, and performance baseline runs.
- Deliverable: Integration signoff checklist and sample workload runbook.

4. Stabilization & Handover (Weeks 4-6)
- Tasks: SLO tuning, cost controls (rate limits, batching), alerting and dashboards, runbook handover.
- Deliverable: Production-ready runbook, monitoring dashboards, support escalation contacts.

5. Ongoing (Post-handover)
- Routine: weekly sync for 30 days, then monthly health checks and quarterly QBRs.

INTEGRATION CHECKLIST (TECHNICAL)

Network & Security
- Confirm IP allowlist or private networking details (VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or PrivateLink).
- TLS required for all endpoints (mutual TLS when requested for Private deployments).
- KMS/HSM integration plan for Private or Dedicated customers; provide key policy and rotation schedule.

Authentication & Authorization
- API keys vs SSO: recommend API keys for service-to-service; SSO/OAuth for human dashboards.
- Provision initial API key scoped with minimal permissions for validation.
- Configure RBAC for production users (roles: admin, ops, dev, read-only).

API & Webhook Integration
- Recommended rate limits and retry patterns: exponential backoff with jitter; max 5 retries, 30s base backoff.
- Sample cURL for basic generation request:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{"model":"redwood-1", "input":"Hello"}'

- Webhook considerations: delivery guarantees are best-effort, ensure idempotency on the receiver side.

Model & Performance Configuration
- Suggested initial model and quantization profile based on workload (see internal quantization-profiles page).
- Warm-up runs: execute 50-100 short requests to populate KV caches for latency-sensitive workloads.
- Batching: enable continuous batching for high-throughput routes; tune max_batch_latency to balance latency and cost.

Data Handling & Privacy
- Verify PII flows and data retention settings; provide retention policy and purge controls for customer data.
- For regulated customers, confirm log scrubbing and audit logging retention window.

INTEGRATION VALIDATION TESTS
- Connectivity test: verify API and webhook reachability from customer network.
- Auth test: key or SSO login success and RBAC enforcement checks.
- Throughput and latency baseline: 95th percentile latency and tokens/sec targets recorded.
- Output quality smoke tests with curated prompt sets; compare against baseline metrics in the eval-harness.

ESCALATION PLAYBOOK

Severity definitions & SLAs
- Severity 1 (Sev1): Production outage for customer-facing features (SLO: initial respond 15 min, engineer engaged 1 hour, resolution or mitigation plan 4 hours).
- Severity 2 (Sev2): Significant degradation for a subset of users or major functionality (SLO: initial respond 30 min, mitigation plan 8 business hours).
- Severity 3 (Sev3): Non-critical issues or configuration questions (SLO: respond 8 business hours).

Escalation ladder
1. Triage (Support Level 1) - confirm scope, collect logs, assign ticket, attempt standard mitigations.
2. SE/Implementation - engage for integration, auth, or configuration failures; run live tests with customer.
3. SRE / Platform - engage for latency, capacity, or cluster-level issues. Open incident if cross-customer.
4. Engineering (Runtime / Model) - for reproducible regressions, model quality regressions, or kernel/runtime bugs.

Required artifacts when escalating
- Full request/response payload (redact PII if required).
- Timestamped trace IDs and route IDs.
- Metrics snapshot: latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, and token consumption for the affected timeframe.
- Steps to reproduce and a minimum failing test case.

On-call playbook steps (example Sev1)
1. Support collects tickets and confirms impact with customer.
2. If impact > 1 customer or causes data loss, SRE opens an incident and posts to #incidents.
3. Notify execs and account team per notify matrix when incident is unresolved after 1 hour.
4. Provide hourly status updates to customer until mitigation; publish postmortem after incident closure.

KNOWN ISSUES & WORKAROUNDS (Enterprise-focused)

1. 401 Unauthorized after key rotation
- Symptom: client requests start failing with 401 immediately after key rotation.
- Root cause: client uses long-lived cached key or proxy caches old key.
- Workaround: confirm new key propagated; purge key caches on proxies; instruct client to re-authenticate.

2. Latency spikes during autoscaling events
- Symptom: 95th percentile latency increases for 5-15 minutes after scale-up.
- Root cause: cold KV cache and model warm-up on new replicas.
- Workaround: pre-warm replicas with short requests during expected scale events; increase burst capacity setting.

3. Embedding drift / semantic mismatch after model swap
- Symptom: similarity searches degrade after switching model version.
- Root cause: embedding space differs between model versions.
- Workaround: re-embed corpus with new model; use scoring thresholds and run A/B tests during rollout.

4. Webhook duplicate deliveries
- Symptom: downstream receives duplicate webhook events.
- Root cause: retries combined with non-idempotent consumer logic.
- Workaround: include idempotency keys and dedupe on consumer side; switch webhook to at-least-once handling.

SUPPORT PROCESS & TEMPLATES

Ticket triage flow
- Step 1: Intake (Support L1) - confirm customer, severity, and obtain artifacts.
- Step 2: Reproduce - attempt to reproduce in staging or with customer-provided data.
- Step 3: Triage routing - assign to SE, SRE, or Engineering as appropriate with required artifacts.
- Step 4: Communicate - provide customer-centric status updates using templates below.

Customer update template (initial)
- Greeting and acknowledgement of receipt.
- Summary of issue and severity classification.
- Actions taken so far and data requested (trace IDs, recent request IDs).
- Expected next update time and primary contact.

Escalation request template (internal)
- Ticket ID, customer name, severity, summary, reproduction steps, and attached artifacts.

HEALTH CHECKS, METRICS & QBR MATERIALS

Key metrics to monitor (weekly)
- Request volume (requests/min) and token consumption (tokens/min)
- Latency p50/p90/p95 (ms)
- Error rate (5xx, 4xx) and per-route error breakdown
- Cost per 1k tokens and estimated monthly spend vs committed usage
- Model quality signals: top-5 prompt failure rate from smoke tests, hallucination flags

Health check runbook (30-day cadence)
- Weekly for first 30 days: CS + SE review dashboards and critical alerts.
- Monthly: cost review, SLO adherence, and usage trend analysis.
- Quarterly (QBR): business metrics, model performance, roadmap alignment, and action plan.

QBR agenda (60-90 minutes)
1. Introductions and objectives (5 min)
2. Business goals recap and key metrics (10 min)
3. Technical health and performance (20 min)
   - Latency, errors, throughput, incident review
4. Cost and optimization opportunities (10 min)
   - Batching, quantization recommendations, caching
5. Feature roadmap and upcoming changes (10 min)
6. Action items and next steps (5-10 min)

QBR deliverables
- Executive summary slide (1 page)
- Technical appendix with dashboards and runbooks
- Action item tracker with owners and due dates

TEMPLATES & CHECKLISTS

- Integration signoff checklist (use during stabilization): a short checklist covering network, auth, SLOs, alerts, and runbooks.
- Incident handoff checklist for postmortems: timelines, mitigation steps, customer communication history, and follow-up items.
- QBR slide template: executive summary, metrics, observations, recommendations, and action tracker.
